instructions.title: Prepare Your Workspace and Tools
instructions.text: Ensure your cutting board is clean and stable. Sharpen your sashimi knife (yanagiba) for precise cuts. Prepare a bowl of ice water with a clean cloth for wiping your knife frequently to prevent fish oils from dulling the blade and affecting flavor. Gather all garnishes and dipping sauces.

instructions.title: Prepare Garnishes
instructions.text: Peel the daikon radish and slice it into very thin rounds, then julienne them into fine strands (tsuma). Rinse the daikon tsuma in cold water and drain well. Arrange shiso leaves, daikon tsuma, and lemon wedges on your serving platter, creating a beautiful base for your sashimi. Have your wasabi and pickled ginger ready.

instructions.title: Slice Tuna and Salmon
instructions.text: Pat the tuna and salmon blocks dry with paper towels. Position the fish on your cutting board with the skin side (if any was present) facing away from you. Using long, smooth, single strokes with your sharp sashimi knife, slice the tuna and salmon against the grain into approximately 1/4 inch thick pieces. Wipe your knife clean after every few cuts.

instructions.title: Slice Yellowtail and Scallops
instructions.text: For yellowtail, slice similarly to tuna and salmon, against the grain, about 1/4 inch thick. For scallops, if large, slice horizontally into 2-3 discs. If smaller, they can be served whole. Arrange these carefully on your platter, considering color and texture balance with the other fish.

instructions.title: Arrange Sweet Shrimp and Final Touches
instructions.text: Carefully arrange the sweet shrimp (amaebi) on the platter. You can gently curl them or lay them flat. Add any optional edible flowers or microgreens for an extra touch of elegance. Ensure there is visual appeal and a variety of colors and textures across the platter.

instructions.title: Serve with Accompaniments
instructions.text: Present the Sashimi Omakase Platter immediately. Serve with small individual dishes of soy sauce for dipping. Encourage guests to add a tiny dab of wasabi directly to each sashimi piece before dipping for the best flavor experience. Offer pickled ginger as a palate cleanser between different types of fish.

tips: Always use the freshest, highest-quality sashimi-grade fish from a reputable fishmonger. The quality of your ingredients is paramount for sashimi.
A very sharp knife is crucial for clean, precise sashimi cuts. Dull knives will tear the fish, affecting both appearance and texture. Consider investing in a dedicated sashimi knife.
Serve sashimi immediately after preparing to ensure optimal freshness and temperature. Keep your platter chilled until serving, ideally on a bed of ice if serving outdoors or in a warm environment.
